# Tournament Requirements Checklist: Gestion de tournois de cube

**Purpose**: Review whether tournament, pairing, persistence, security and UX requirements are complete and unambiguous before implementation
**Created**: 2026-09-21
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the actor and access expectations complete for collaborative guild administration, including the explicit absence of per-tournament ownership? [Completeness, Spec §FR-020, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK002 Are lifecycle requirements complete for preparation, active and completed tournaments, including which mutations remain allowed after completion? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, FR-014, FR-016]
- [ ] CHK003 Are participant requirements complete for creation, removal before start, withdrawal after start and remaining forfeits? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 1, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK004 Are cube requirements complete for selection, replacement before start, immutable snapshot identity and historical reconstruction? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, FR-005, FR-016]
- [ ] CHK005 Are Deck déclaré requirements complete for name, manual Cartes clés and behavior after tournament completion, with photo recognition explicitly excluded? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, FR-017–FR-018, Scope]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the default round-count rule documented for every supported participant count and format, while preserving the organizer's pre-start override? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 Is “éviter les rencontres déjà jouées lorsque possible” defined precisely enough to distinguish a globally avoidable rematch from a locally greedy choice? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, Plan §Appariements et classement]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the first-round ordering requirement explicit about reproducible pseudo-randomness, seed persistence and the absence of registration-order bias? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, Plan §Appariements et classement]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the distinction between Exemption suisse and Pause toutes-rondes explicit for pairing, points, games and opponent averages? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, FR-012]
- [ ] CHK010 Are valid played, drawn and forfeit score shapes defined without leaving “score valide” open to incompatible interpretations? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK011 Are OMW%, GWP% and OGW% definitions explicit about the 33.33% floor, bye exclusion, empty averages and exact comparison before rounding? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the effect of a late correction stated unambiguously for current standings, future rounds and already published rounds? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014, Edge Cases]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK013 Are collaborative access requirements consistent between the actor description, FR-020, assumptions and the HTTP contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020, Contracts §HTTP Control]
- [ ] CHK014 Are three-player pause semantics consistent across the user story, functional requirements, success criteria and domain glossary? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 4, FR-009, SC-004]
- [ ] CHK015 Are snapshot timing requirements consistent between editable setup, start-time locking, database archive and historical key-card validation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, FR-016–FR-017]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the exclusion of photo recognition consistent across scope, requirements, contracts, data model and tasks, with Issue #81 as the only follow-up pointer? [Consistency, Spec §Scope, Research §9]
- [ ] CHK017 Are the 2–32 participant limit, recommended round counts and five-round scope mutually consistent for all supported formats? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, Assumptions, SC-002]
- [ ] CHK018 Are post-completion key-card edits and result corrections consistent with the meaning of a completed but still auditable tournament? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014–FR-018]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK019 Can the three-minute creation outcome be measured with a defined start/end and a representative organizer/cube setup? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK020 Can the no-avoidable-rematch requirement be objectively established against an independent existence check for 2–32 participants? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002, FR-007]
- [ ] CHK021 Can deterministic reconstruction be independently assessed from stored inputs, events, seed and engine version without relying on the checkpoint implementation? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK022 Are durable-history acceptance criteria strong enough to distinguish committed PostgreSQL storage from in-memory, browser or best-effort local storage? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-007, Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK023 Are keyboard and 360 px requirements defined for every critical state: empty history, setup, active round, conflict, completed history and card selection? [Coverage, Spec §FR-019, FR-022, SC-008]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK024 Are concurrent start, concurrent result and idempotent retry scenarios all specified with winner, loser and no-mutation outcomes? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Plan §Persistance]
- [ ] CHK025 Are database outage, timeout, restart and partial transaction requirements specified, including the prohibition on silent local fallback? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-024, Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK026 Are requirements complete for correcting a prior result after one or more later rounds are already published? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, FR-014]
- [ ] CHK027 Are withdrawal and forfeit requirements clear for already published matches, future rounds and final standings? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK028 Are empty, loading, stale-revision and no-history UI states intentionally specified or explicitly deferred? [Gap, Spec §User Scenarios]
- [ ] CHK029 Are duplicate names, blank deck names, invalid cube identities and out-of-range participant counts covered by observable rejection requirements? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1, FR-002–FR-006]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK030 Are pairing, mutation and history-list performance targets tied to stated scale and a reproducible measurement environment? [Clarity, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK031 Are authorization requirements explicit that browser roles cannot write tournament tables directly and that all mutations cross the protected server seam? [Security, Plan §Persistance et concurrence]
- [ ] CHK032 Is the no-expiration/no-deletion policy defined consistently for tournament history, command receipts and archived snapshots? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK033 Are recovery requirements complete for empty history, loading, store failure and stale revision while preserving unconfirmed input? [Coverage, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK034 Are observability requirements defined for store failures, revision conflicts, forced rematches and latency without logging credentials or tournament secrets? [Coverage, Spec §FR-023]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK035 Is the requirement to archive full cube snapshots justified and scoped for cubes that currently lack immutable snapshot files? [Dependency, Spec §FR-016–FR-017, Research §6]
- [ ] CHK036 Is the production dependency on PostgreSQL/Supabase distinguished from the explicit test/development memory adapter in all delivery claims? [Assumption, Spec §Dependencies, Plan §Storage]
- [ ] CHK037 Are deviations from homologated Magic/EventLink behavior clearly disclosed, especially participant minimums, round presets and DraftMaster-specific pairings? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, Research §1]
- [ ] CHK038 Is Issue #81 clearly separated so no vision provider, upload contract or photo field is required by feature 008? [Dependency, Spec §Scope, Research §9]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline and link to the exact corrected requirement when resolving a gap.
